about: The line contract of mrk's five --check modes, as data. For each case: the fields, and the line that mrk_check_line in scripts/lib.sh writes for them, without its newline. A reader that undoes the escapes gets the fields back from the line. It splits an output into lines only at a newline, and each line into fields only at a tab. sevmorris/mrk keeps this file at tests/fixtures/check-lines.json and writes its lines with MRK_UPDATE_FIXTURES=1 go test in tools/mrk-status. Dipstick and Barkeep keep a copy, byte for byte, which mrk's tests compare. Do not edit a line by hand.

cases.why: Each of the three escapes: a tab, a newline and a backslash.
Empty fields: one between two fields, and one at the end.
A field that is only a backslash, and a field that ends in one.
Text that looks like an escape: a backslash before t, before n and before a backslash.

A carriage return, which mrk_check_line does not escape: alone, inside a field, and at the end of the last field. A reader that splits the output into lines by Swift Character joins this line to the next.
A combining mark after an escaped tab, backslash and newline. A reader that walks Swift Characters joins the mark to the escape, and then cannot read the line.
Text outside ASCII, with an accent composed and decomposed.
Characters that a shell or HTML gives a meaning to.
